staged_record.description_long: In Otto v. City of Boca Raton, a divided U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit panel ruled in November 2020 that ordinances adopted by Boca Raton and Palm Beach County restricting licensed therapists from providing conversion therapy to minors violated the First Amendment. The majority concluded that the local rules regulated speech and could not survive the constitutional review applied in the case. Judge Beverly Martin dissented, arguing that the ordinances regulated professional conduct and that the ruling would hinder local efforts to protect minors from a harmful practice. The decision was an appellate ruling about two Florida local ordinances and the speech rights of therapists; it did not establish a national policy or invalidate every conversion-therapy restriction. The Trump-appointed-judges framing in the original title is not necessary to state the holding and does not itself explain the legal reasoning. A precise entry should name the court, municipalities, date, and divided nature of the decision, while keeping the holding limited to the case before the panel.
